summary: tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1 now has a standing EndingObeysSkip mutant. It is in the -Mutant ValidateSet and in the hard-coded -Mutant All roster. Its $CaseMutants entry targets L-002 and MainWindow.xaml.cs, and uses the spike's Find/Replace verbatim ('else if (!ReferenceEquals(final, _shownTopLevel))' gets '&& !_skipNextRefresh'). Its one Fail pattern is the topLevel.final line, and an Expect line pins actual 'False'. The shared Test-CaseMutant gained one optional key, MayFail. It sets aside the reading/bytes/files FAIL lines, which follow from the mutant on most runs but not all. Without it the harness could never count this mutant as killed. The acceptance test now exits 0. -Mutant EndingObeysSkip exits 0 through the real harness: it publishes the mutated app in a scratch copy and L-002 fails on topLevel.final False. -Mutant All passes all 9 mutants in 338 s. A new tests/bugs/SL-064-MutantCases.ps1 feeds each owed shape (C-001..C-008).

files.why: Adds 'EndingObeysSkip' to the -Mutant ValidateSet, the header list and the -Mutant All roster. Adds the $CaseMutants['EndingObeysSkip'] entry: L-002, MainWindow.xaml.cs, the spike's Find/Replace, the Fail pattern for topLevel.final, MayFail for the reading/bytes/files symptoms, and Expect actual 'False'. Test-CaseMutant now sets aside FAIL lines that match an entry's optional MayFail before its exact 'Fail and nothing else' comparison. Entries without MayFail behave exactly as before.

The slice's case script, -Case C-001..C-008 or All. It loads WindowMutants.ps1's own definitions (parsed from the file, not re-typed) into a private module and feeds each owed shape. C-001..C-006 need no build and finish in seconds. C-007 and C-008 publish the app in the harness's scratch copy and take about 1 minute each. ASCII only, and it parses under both 5.1 and 7.

obligations.how: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/bugs/SL-064-EndingObeysSkipMutant.Tests.ps1 now exits 0 ('OK: WindowMutants.ps1 has a standing EndingObeysSkip mutant for L-002...'). The acceptance test itself was not modified. The obligation is owed to validate-slice, which will re-run it.

C-001 passes -Mutant EndingObeysSkip through WindowMutants.ps1's real param block (taken from its AST) and it binds. -Mutant All still binds, and 'EndingObeysSkipX' is refused with ParameterBindingValidationException. Against HEAD's WindowMutants.ps1 this case fails with the ValidateSet error.

C-002 queries $CaseMutants['EndingObeysSkip'] in the loaded harness and checks: Case is L-002, File equals $MainWindow and exists, WindowCases.ps1 defines Test-L002, and the run loop sends the name to Test-CaseMutant (it is in $CaseMutants and there is no Test-EndingObeysSkip).

C-003 checks that the anchor matches once in the whole of MainWindow.xaml.cs and that the match lies inside ShowFinalTopLevel. It then runs the harness's own Set-Mutation on a copy and checks that everything before and after ShowFinalTopLevel, RefreshTopLevel included, is byte-identical. Two further shapes: the anchor planted twice, and the anchor reformatted. Set-Mutation refuses both ('matches 2 times' / 'matches 0 times') and leaves the file alone.

C-004 takes the real and the mutated ShowFinalTopLevel text verbatim and compiles each with Add-Type, with stub fields and counted ShowTopLevel/ClearTopLevel. With _skipNextRefresh true and a new final snapshot, the real guard shows it and the mutant leaves the earlier snapshot. With no skip armed both show it, and both clear on null. An inert Replace (no _skipNextRefresh) turns C-004 red. C-007 also shows the real run ending with the skip armed ('ok the next skip was armed when Cancel was pressed').

C-005 feeds the real Test-CaseMutant L-002 outputs through an overridden Invoke-ScratchCase; Set-Mutation still runs for real. Killed: the full reading/bytes/files/final signature, and final alone. Not killed: L-002 passed, final held, final '<null>' instead of 'False', hook never acted, app crash (exit -532462766 / no report), mutated app did not publish. Without MayFail the full-signature shape goes red, which is why the deviation exists.

C-006 evaluates WindowMutants.ps1's own $names statement with $Mutant='All'. It contains EndingObeysSkip, every other ValidateSet name, each once. With $Mutant='EndingObeysSkip' it contains that name alone. A real -Mutant All run also passed: all 9 mutants, exit 0, 338 s.

C-007 runs WindowMutants.ps1 -Mutant EndingObeysSkip for real and requires all of the following: exit 0 and PASSED: EndingObeysSkip; 'publishing the app' inside the scratch copy; the skip armed; L-002 printing the topLevel.final FAIL line with actual 'False'; FAILED: L-002; the harness's Fail match; the real MainWindow.xaml.cs hash unchanged; the scratch copy removed. It passed in 52 s. The same run was made directly twice more: 55 s standalone and inside -Mutant All.

C-008 uses the harness's own New-Scratch to make an unmutated copy (its MainWindow.xaml.cs hash equals the real one) and its own Invoke-ScratchCase to publish and run L-002. Result: exit 0, PASSED: L-002, no FAIL line, the skip armed at the ending, topLevel.final held. Remove-Scratch removed the copy and the real source was unchanged. It passed in 53 s.

This is owed to validate-slice, but the evidence exists now. Test-CaseMutant counts a kill only when three things hold: exit 1, 'FAILED: L-002' printed, and the non-MayFail FAIL lines are exactly the topLevel.final line, with actual 'False' shown. C-005 feeds it a publish failure (compile error, no FAILED: L-002), an app crash, a hook that never acted, and a missing final. None counts as killed. The real run killed it for the specific signal. Validate should still re-run -Mutant EndingObeysSkip itself.

deviations: The design said the entry needs 'exactly one Fail pattern' and that the harness 'exits 0 only when L-002 fails specifically on the topLevel.final line'. But the existing Test-CaseMutant requires the case's FAIL lines to equal the Fail list exactly, in count and order ('failed on /.../ and nothing else'). The real mutant run prints four FAIL lines: topLevel.reading, bytes, files and final. With one Fail pattern, the harness as written would report the mutant as not killed on every run. Listing all four would instead miss the spike's 1-in-20 run. The smallest fix was an optional per-entry MayFail key in Test-CaseMutant: FAIL lines matching it are set aside before the exact comparison. Entries without MayFail behave exactly as before (-Mutant All re-proved all 8 existing mutants). Fail stays the single topLevel.final pattern the design asked for. MayFail is limited to the three L-002 figures that follow from a stale snapshot, so a crash, a hook failure, a publish failure or any other FAIL line still prevents a kill (C-005 shows this).

Added Expect = actual 'False' to the entry. It uses the existing Expect mechanism and is not in the design. It keeps a report whose final field is missing ('<null>') from counting as the specific signal, in line with the design's own positive-control rule. C-005 covers that shape.
follow_ups: The -Mutant All roster in WindowMutants.ps1 is still a hard-coded list next to the ValidateSet. C-006 guards it for this slice, but deriving it from the ValidateSet (minus 'All') would stop a future mutant from being reachable by name yet missing from All.
The bug report was only a title. The build assumed its intent from the repro test and the design: a standing mutant in WindowMutants.ps1, not a change to the app.
eng/dotnet.ps1 installed SDK 10.0.401 into this worktree's gitignored .dotnet/ (per Q-003), because the machine has only 8.0/9.0. Each worktree installs its own copy (~300 MB).
